detail.hypothesis: Explicit instance ownership and paired offsets remove an exact-program representability ceiling that token and piano-roll states alias.
Copy-by-default sparse edits preserve correct baseline mass that full replacement decoders destroy.
Separating event existence, timing, and scene-roster identity decisions avoids destructive coupling inside one joint token decision.
Latent source objects constrained by transcription and remix consistency expose ownership evidence hidden in a mixture waveform.
Continuously active, dormant/re-entering, and arrangement-level sources require three distinct temporal states that window-local decoding cannot represent.
Compositional GM attributes, retrieved timbre prototypes, and many-to-many vocabulary transport can bind unseen acoustic evidence to a frozen exact-GM target without lossy aliases.
Source add-remove counterfactuals on admitted real mixtures provide ownership supervision absent from synthetic-only or marginal labels.
Global acoustic energy, posterior decision risk, and counterfactual note contribution expose scene errors that token-local scores cannot distinguish.
Fixed local proposal cardinality causes deletion errors as density rises; adaptive allocation can recover events without buying recall through false additions.
Separately marginalizing time alignment, program-confusion, and event-presence observation processes prevents fitting one noisy annotation while preserving a fixed primary estimand.
